items.summary: The UN migration agency has reported that at least 139 people were killed and 84 remain missing after a migrant boat sank overnight on its way to Yemen. At least 80 Ethiopians survived the incident but 15 children died.

items.summary: Prime Minister Donald Tusk confirmed the arrest hours after police received information about a possible assassination plot. Poland is still reeling from a wave of school violence this week.

items.summary: Germany's foreign minister has said Berlin is behind Ukraine's president and will keep pressuring Russia to end its war. Meanwhile, Deutsche Bank's CEO warned that political extremism is spooking investors. More on DW.

items.title: Surrogacy in Georgia is booming, but at what cost?
items.summary: Georgia became a hub for surrogate pregnancies after Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022. DW spoke with parents, and those who wanted to become parents, about the hidden costs of a booming industry.

items.title: Germany's population is shrinking, but not everywhere
items.summary: By 2045, Germany will have more older people, fewer workers and a smaller population overall. Yet some regions will defy this trend. Their success depends on how much they have to offer.

items.title: India's 'Cockroach' movement leaders say 'the fight has just begun' after a large protest in Delhi
items.summary: Leaders of the youth-led protest movement demanding India's election commissioner step down say the "fight has just begun" after they were released from detention following a large demonstration in Delhi. More on DW.

items.summary: The Department of Justice is investigating whether the five news organizations violated antitrust laws when they suspended their coverage of Trump in protest. The networks under probe are ABC, CBS, CNN, NBC and Fox News.

items.summary: The storm, which is now a post-tropical cyclone, had made landfall near Destin, Florida on Friday evening. The storm brings heavy rainfall and powerful winds and has caused mass power outages in Florida and Alabama.

items.title: Palestinian president postpones elections until late 2027
items.summary: Palestinian President Mahmoud Abbas previously committed to holding legislative elections in November 2026. He said that due to "obstacles ⁠posed by Israeli measures" the vote would be pushed back until late next year.

items.title: Saudi Arabia: 12 killed, hundreds injured in Riyadh airport attack

items.summary: The US is holding Congress and state governor elections. At all levels of US politics, women are underrepresented — but they may win some historic victories in the midterms on November 3.

items.summary: Eritrea has officially requested UN Security Council assistance over the conflict in Tigray. Both Eritrea and Ethiopia accuse each other of fueling regional instability.

items.summary: Already named the 2025 Oxford Word of the Year, "rage bait" has also been widely adopted in German slang.

items.summary: How prepared is Germany for national defense? The answer lies in the Operations Plan Germany. Military exercises such as "Red Storm Charlie" are designed to put these preparations to the test in realistic scenarios.

items.title: Schools crisis in France: Investment fails to inspire confidence
items.summary: For weeks, schoolchildren in France have been protesting the failing education system. Compared to many other countries, France invests heavily in education but critics say that the funds are not distributed fairly.

items.title: Macron and Steinmeier struggle to revive Franco-German ties
items.summary: Presidents Frank-Walter Steinmeier and Emmanuel Macron are about to step down from their offices. Their meeting in France made it clear how urgently the Franco-German partnership needs new momentum.

items.title: Author or artificial intelligence? Literature in crisis
items.summary: AI is a hot topic at this year's Frankfurt Book Fair. An international literary scandal has raised questions about machine-generated texts.

items.summary: The Belarusian musician and civil rights activist Maria Kalesnikava held the keynote speech on the importance of art at the 2026 Beethovenfest in Bonn. She also visited DW.

items.title: Poland: Lifeline for Ukrainian refugees confronts donor fatigue and online abuse as anti-Ukrainian sentiment grows
items.summary: A Ukrainian woman who fled the war in her country built a lifeline for refugees in Poland. Now her organization faces donor fatigue, funding cuts and rising hostility as support for Ukrainians in Poland wanes.

items.title: World Cup 2034: Does Saudi Arabia shelving Neom Stadium spell trouble?
items.summary: Since winning the right to hold the 2034 World Cup unopposed, Saudi Arabia has been pulling away from sport. With reports that its most ambitious stadium project will be abandoned, what does this mean for the World Cup?

items.title: Germany women's football team: Can Ena Mahmutovic make a case to become Germany's next No.1 goalkeeper?
items.summary: The women's friendlies against Australia and Japan present an opportunity for Ena Mahmutovic to make her case for succeeding Ann-Katrin Berger as Germany's first-choice goalkeeper.

items.title: Bosnia-Herzegovina will soon have a new grand mufti
items.summary: The new leader of the Islamic Community in Bosnia-Herzegovina will be elected on October 10. The reis-ul-ulema's role is not only important for Muslims in the country itself, but could inspire Muslims across Europe.

items.title: Finland, the world's happiest nation, faces a glum winter
items.summary: Finns have many reasons to feel content, but the country's pile of debt is not one of them. Russia's war in Ukraine has added to the fiscal burden. Can the Nordic nation absorb another shock?

items.title: EU pulls sponsorship from Disinfo2026 event in Lithuania
items.summary: The EU's diplomatic service, Canada and host nation Lithuania all pulled support from a disinformation event in Vilnius. Amid reports of US pressure, the EU said it was "uncomfortable with the framing" of some panels.

items.summary: The works of this year's Nobel Prize-winning poet and essayist Anne Carson can feel slightly daunting. Here are some keys to understanding her universe.

items.title: Early-onset cancer rising worldwide: Causes, risk, prevention
items.summary: Across Latin America, early-onset cancer rates have risen, especially of bowel, breast and cervical cancers. But it is a worldwide trend.

items.title: Germany news: UK's Burnham visits Berlin for talks with Merz
items.summary: UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham is visiting Berlin to launch a new bilateral treaty and hold talks with Chancellor Friedrich Merz. President Steinmeier is on a state visit to France.

items.title: Security in the Black Sea region: is Bulgaria the weak link in Europe's defense against threats from Russia?
items.summary: Two ships have sunk off the coast of Bulgaria and Romania after drone attacks in recent days. Bulgaria has held back on pointing the finger at Russia. What does that mean for security in the Black Sea and the region?

items.title: How a multibillion-dollar oilfield has ignited the UK-Argentina feud over the Falklands
items.summary: Argentina and the UK once fought a war over the Falkland Islands. Now, the multibillion-dollar Sea Lion oil project has reignited old tensions, with Buenos Aires seeking to put a stop to the plans.

items.title: Nobel Prize in literature goes to Canada's Anne Carson
items.summary: Carson won for her "bold and inventive oeuvre." The decorated poet and essayist is known for her reverence for Latin and Greek classics.

items.title: South Korea recalls Ukraine ambassador amid POW dispute
items.summary: South Korea has said it will recall its ambassador to Ukraine. Seoul is upset about a transfer of North Korean prisoners of war being made public knowledge at the UN and had demanded — but not received — an apology.

items.title: As Russia steps up attacks on Ukrainian data centers, could Ukraine soon be offline?
items.summary: As Russia targets Ukraine's data centers more and more, experts say the country's internet system is too robust to shut down entirely. However, services could become more expensive.

items.title: German Bundeswehr: A new naval port in Emden aims to enhance Germany's defense capabilities
items.summary: Citing the escalating security threat, Germany's Navy has decided to establish a second port on the North Sea coast. Emden was chosen as the location.

items.title: Middle Corridor: Can Bulgaria be a safe gateway for Asian imports to the EU?
items.summary: The EU wants more trade via the Middle Corridor, which could bring big benefits for Bulgaria. But Tuesday's drone attacks on commercial ships off the Bulgarian coast are a stark reminder of the security risks involved.

items.title: Gerhard Schröder visits latest Russian employer, Hyperglobus
items.summary: Former German Chancellor Gerhard Schröder visited a Moscow supermarket in his new role on the supervisory board. Schröder is no stranger to retirement stipends in Russia — or the scandal that accompanies them.

items.title: '90s art scene in the UK: An international, edgy trendsetter
items.summary: The 1990s are remembered for Brit-pop and provocative fashion, but beyond the nostalgia, it was a decade of cultural experimentation and social change. Tate Britain's new exhibition looks past the familiar icons.

items.title: Germany news: Merz rails against extremism, AfD sympathizers
items.summary: Political extremism threatens Germany's existing social order, Chancellor Merz has said. The Transport Ministry has proposed a five-year plan to improve Germany's ailing railroad infrastructure.

items.summary: The European Commission is proposing earlier access to EU markets for candidate countries, new voting rules to reduce vetoes and extra safeguards for a bigger bloc. But is the reform fair — or even feasible?

items.title: German spy scandal threatens national security
items.summary: The arrest of Germany's former intelligence chief August Hanning could undermine national security, experts warn, as allies may reconsider their intelligence relationships.

items.title: Germany: Did CDU lawmakers support the far-right AfD?
items.summary: Lawmakers of the center-right CDU may have voted for the far-right AfD candidate for parliamentary speaker in Saxony-Anhalt. Germany's Social Democrats warn of a "unique breach of taboos."

items.title: Nobel Prize in chemistry goes to Henri B. Kagan and Kenso Soai
items.summary: Henri B. Kagan and Kenso Soai won the Nobel Prize in chemistry for their groundbreaking discoveries related to the origin of chirality and life's building blocks.

items.title: Suspected pneumonic plague in Siberia: What we know about the disease
items.summary: After a worker at a Russian plague research institute in Siberia died October 2, 2026, nearly 200 of her contacts were under medical observation. But authorities there denied pneumonic plague had caused the death.

items.title: Ronaldo stays on under cloud as Messi exits internationals
items.summary: Just hours before Lionel Messi played his last match for Argentina, Cristiano Ronaldo posted his latest salvo in a row with Portugal. Ronaldo wants to play on despite the troubles, while Messi bathed in adulation.

items.title: Nobelitis — How winning a Nobel Prize can give you delusions of grandeur
items.summary: After being chosen for one of the world's most prestigious awards, some Nobel laureates lose touch with reality and suddenly start spouting unscientific nonsense. They're afflicted by what some have called "Nobelitis."

items.title: Emerging economies are embracing solar power and skipping fossil fuels much faster than Europe or the US
items.summary: Renewable electricity is cheaper than ever. While the West got rich on coal and oil, some of the world's poorest countries are banking on solar, wind and water instead.

items.title: Where is Spain headed after the snap election announcement?
items.summary: Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez is taking a gamble by calling an early election in Spain. The housing crisis, migration and the rise of the right-wing populist Vox party are all likely to dominate the campaign.

items.title: Munich up against at least six competitors for 2036 Olympics

items.title: EU seeks ways to make expansion more palatable to members
items.summary: The European Commission has put forward ideas it hopes will both ease the EU expansion process and allay concerns among existing members. Several countries, not least war-torn Ukraine, are among the candidates.

items.title: France's conundrum: How to cut spending amid protests
items.summary: Prime Minister Lecornu is pledging to improve schools at a time when the government seeks to save billions. France's dilemma can be seen across the EU: How to cut spending when citizens are demanding more from the state?

items.title: Paramount and Warner Bros merge into one Hollywood giant
items.summary: Paramount has completed an $81 billion purchase of Warner Bros. Discovery, as its owner Skydance creates a new entertainment behemoth. Billionaire David Ellison's hostile takeover bid defeated rival efforts from Netflix.

items.title: Germany's far-right AfD makes history again in Saxony-Anhalt

items.title: Fact check: Misleading claims spark plague fears in Russia
items.summary: The death of a lab worker at a plague research institute in Russia has sparked claims about a lab accident, hundreds of infections and international spread. Some of these viral narratives are misleading.

items.summary: AI models have repeatedly broken into real commercial and government systems during safety tests during 2026. Cybersecurity researcher Thorsten Holz explains what that means, and why he isn't expecting a robot uprising.

items.title: Germany faces a triple threat from Russia, China and domestic far-right extremists

items.title: Germany news: Far-right AfD gets first house speaker in a German state parliament

items.title: Merz, Macron seek tougher EU measures against unfair trade
items.summary: Emmanuel Macron and Friedrich Merz have written to Ursula von der Leyen, calling for tougher EU mechanisms against unfair trade practices by other states. They name no names but seem to have China or the US in mind.

items.title: Australia, New Zealand probe Flydubai pilot's time there
items.summary: The Flydubai pilot from Oman suspected of trying to crash a plane in Israel spent time in Oceania as a young man. Police in both Australia and New Zealand said they would investigate his links to the countries.

items.title: Euro plummets against US dollar: Has the next financial crisis begun?
items.summary: The euro has fallen to a 17-month low against the dollar. That will make inflation worse in the EU, where political worries and concern over French debt are already troubling investors. Is a fiscal crisis at hand?

items.title: Trust in the German Constitutional Court is eroding — how can this be stopped?
items.summary: Germany's top court, which turned 75 this year, is losing the population's trust, surveys show. Some say reforms in the way it picks candidates would help, to also accept candidates nominated by the far-right AfD.

items.title: Germany news: Spy chief warns Russia conflict risk growing
items.summary: Moscow is already waging a "shadow war" against Europe, the head of Germany's foreign intelligence service says. The Left Party is taking a case over remarks by the CDU's Katherina Reiche to a top court.

items.title: Jürgen Klopp faces myriad of issues after rough start with Germany
items.summary: Jürgen Klopp has done things a little differently since becoming Germany coach. Casting a wider net for talent and trying to connect with players and country haven't made an immediate impact, but he is not bowed.

items.title: Bosnia election: New steps to prevent electoral fraud, but nationalist parties remain on top
items.summary: New technology has stopped votes being cast on behalf of dead or absent voters, and turnout has fallen to a record low. But it was a case of deja vu in Bosnia's elections with the same parties winning.

items.title: Hundreds of French schools shut, teen loses hand in protests
items.summary: The student protests that rocked France last week have prompted authorities to keep up to 500 schools closed on Monday. A teenage boy lost his hand, seemingly while trying to pick up a police tear gas grenade.

items.title: Nationalists top Bosnia-Herzegovina's divisive election
items.summary: Bosnia-Herzegovina's three-member presidency is set to be dominated by nationalists from the three major ethnic groups, including Zeljka ​Cvijanovic, backed by disqualified Serb secessionist leader Milorad Dodik.

items.title: German reunification: How inequality is shaping a new East German identity
items.summary: A new study highlights persistent structural disparities in wealth and leadership positions between East and West Germany, 36 years after reunification.

items.title: "NAZA": Israeli military issues statement on film
items.summary: The award-winning documentary "NAZA" continues to spark controversy in Israel. The Israeli military has now published a multi-page statement calling the film's portrayal "distorted."

items.title: Germany's Franz Reindl elected new IIHF president
items.summary: Franz Reindl has been elected president of ice hockey's world governing body. The former forward was a member of West Germany's Olympic bronze medal-winning team.

items.title: Climate leaders called for solar energy for 'everyone, everywhere' by 2030, but with three years to go, is that goal attainable?
items.summary: Prominent climate leaders have called on governments, businesses, institutions and the public to make a push for solar power before the decade is out, repowering the world with cheap, clean energy. Is that possible?

items.title: Manchester City Premier League charges: What do they mean?
items.summary: Since being bought by the UAE in 2008, Manchester City has become one of the world's most successful football clubs. A raft of serious financial charges threatens to undermine this and bring chaos to the Premier League.

items.title: ARD-Deutschlandtrend survey: Germans unite in frustration over the government

items.title: Turkey: Stock market scandal hits half a million investors
items.summary: Asset managers are alleged to have artificially inflated the value of their funds. Turkish authorities have made multiple arrests, and a leading AKP lawmaker has resigned.

items.title: Klopp wins first game as Germany coach, without 'top dogs'
items.summary: It may have taken a little longer than he would have liked, but Jürgen Klopp has finally won a game as Germany coach. Despite a number of debutants, it was a familiar face who stood out in the victory over Serbia.

items.title: Weakened US fuel-efficiency rules and promises of cheaper cars could see drivers pay higher running costs while also increasing carbon emissions.
items.summary: Weakened US fuel-efficiency rules and promises of cheaper cars could yet see drivers pay higher running costs while increasing planet-heating emissions.

items.title: Germans' biggest fear is the high cost of living, an annual study finds
items.summary: What do Germans fear most in 2026? Wars? Global crises? Wrong. Their biggest concern is the cost of living, which keeps rising.

items.title: Germany news: Merz lauds NATO with Westphalian Peace Prize
items.summary: At a ceremony to honor NATO, the German chancellor warned that Russia will threaten the rest of Europe if it isn't stopped in Ukraine. In other news, the German military will set up its first drone regiment.

items.title: Germany debates alleged antisemitism in the Left Party
items.summary: The Central Council of Jews in Germany thinks the Left Party is dangerous. Other Jews, however, are showing solidarity with the party. How does that add up?

items.title: Senegal's Youth Olympics makes Olympics in Africa 'logical'

items.summary: Oktoberfest is famous the world over for beer, brass band music and Bavarian traditions. But staff are also reporting incidents of racism and sexism, and are taking a stand against discrimination.

items.title: Is US President Donald Trump right to rename AI as 'Super Intelligence'?

items.title: Ireland will boycott Eurovision again because of Israel's participation, but the song contest is still expanding
items.summary: The 2026 Eurovision Song Contest was marred by boycotts in protest against Israel's participation in the midst of its war on Gaza. It still aims to keep growing.

items.summary: Writer Toby Morton is using a new website to amplify allegations in a high-profile sexual assault lawsuit involving seven Cornell students. The reopening of the case is causing an outcry on social media.

items.title: Global trade weathers Iran, Ukraine and Trump's tariffs
items.summary: Over the past six years, COVID, two wars and Donald Trump's tariffs have shaken world trade. With globalization already stalling, is this a temporary shock or the start of a great reversal?

items.summary: Spain's southern coast produces up to 25% of Europe's fruit and vegetables. But amid intensive farming, climate change and illegal wells, the water it takes to grow them is drying up.

items.title: What do Manchester City's charges mean for German football?
items.summary: Manchester City have reportedly been found guilty of major financial rule breaches. What does this mean for German football?

items.title: Will Jürgen Klopp's charisma be enough for Germany?
items.summary: After defeat to Greece, Jürgen Klopp faces the first real test of his tenure as coach of Germany's national men's football team. Can his charisma alone push this group forward?

items.title: Ireland beat Israel 3-0 in Nations League match overshadowed by political controversy
items.summary: Ireland easily beat Israel in a Nations League fixture that 24 hours earlier appeared in doubt. One Irish player pulled out of the match to express his opposition to Israel's actions in the Gaza Strip.

items.title: What would Francis of Assisi make of his fame today?
items.summary: The Catholic saint renounced wealth and fame to become a mendicant friar. Yet throughout history, his teachings and life have inspired popes, Dante and even Mussolini.

items.title: Backlash over data centers tests Europe's AI ambitions
items.summary: Massive data centers needed to run AI are triggering protests across Europe. Their operators counter that they boost digital sovereignty and energy independence.

items.title: DW shows solidarity with Georgians' commitment to democracy
items.summary: Cultural and media professionals in Georgia remain under threat. A DW panel brings together insiders who share their hopes and fears.

items.title: Bundesliga, other top European leagues call for major FIFA reforms
items.summary: The Bundesliga and three other leading European football leagues have said major reforms to world-governing body FIFA are "essential." However, they stopped short of calling for the resignation of boss Gianni Infantino.

items.title: Jürgen Klopp starts Germany job with shaky Netherlands draw
